title: A conclusion tied to its sources
caption: OFFLINE SAMPLE · 11:00 UTC · 100 mph and 51 counties
narration: EvidenceTrail helps an evidence reviewer investigate why a claim changes. This is a local, offline research replay. At eleven hundred UTC, the selected NOAA advisory reports one hundred miles per hour. Florida's emergency order covers fifty one counties. Each quantity names its source and clock policy.

title: One missing source changes 51 to 35
caption: Simulated withdrawal · original records stay unchanged
narration: Now remove Florida emergency order two fifteen in a controlled simulation. The order claim changes from fifty one to thirty five counties, and the replacement document is named. This shows the computation's source dependence. It does not mean a publisher retracted the document, or establish real world causation.

title: Strict policy abstains
caption: Original publication availability remains unproved
narration: A source's displayed date does not independently prove when its original bytes first became public. Under strict policy, EvidenceTrail abstains and names the missing availability evidence. It does not convert an archive accessible today into proof that the same information was available at the historical decision time.

title: Single-source tests can miss a dependency
caption: FICTIONAL warehouse · two current records share the same issuer
narration: The fictional warehouse illustrates a different failure mode. Two current records support twenty five pallets. Either record alone can preserve that quantity, so a single source test can miss the dependency. The investigator reports the smallest changing groups within its declared search bound. These fictional records do not establish independent corroboration.

title: Withdraw both current records: 25 to 12
caption: Exact source-set experiment · bounded search
narration: Withdraw both current warehouse records. The conclusion changes from twenty five to twelve pallets. The interface exposes the before and after values, the exact missing source set, and the checks actually executed. An analyst can inspect why the result changed rather than relying on an untested narrative explanation.

title: Create and review a new case
caption: Operator-declared entries · generated pins check consistency
narration: The same workflow accepts a new case through source entry. Enter a quantity, issuer, reference, excerpt and an exact timestamp, or a printed date with its offset. Preview shows the actual admission clock. Generated hashes record these entries; they do not authenticate a publisher. Explicit review is required before adopting the case.

title: Add evidence at the same review boundary
caption: Reviewed source addition · 73 to 92 pallets
narration: Add a separately reviewed source to the adopted case. Here the quantity changes from seventy three to ninety two pallets. Original records remain intact, and both results use the same captured clock and evidence policy. This is an operator update. It does not silently execute a model call or collect a new source from the internet.

title: Execution evidence and remaining limits
caption: Sponsor runs are separate · local Nightshift adapter probe completed · analyst n = 0
narration: The evidence register separates executions. Earlier runs consumed two real local Zetaris query results and exercised the official Meterless H MEM reference engine. One accepted NVIDIA Nemotron response used the direct provider route. A later EvidenceTrail adapter request completed through a local Nightshift Llama lane with a matching Runtime receipt. This is separate from the offline browser verdict. Independent analyst impact remains unmeasured, and organizer eligibility is unresolved.
